newsitem.title: USA: Fed could add reserves via system RPs - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Fed could add reserves via system RPs - analysts.

text.p: The Federal Reserve could add temporary reserves to the banking system on Tuesday through two-day system repurchase agreements, analysts said.
"We think they could do two-day system repurchases," said Marilyn Schaja, money market analyst at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette.

Patricia Thrapp, vice president at Aubrey G. Lanston, said Treasury balances at the Fed appear to have been lower than analysts had expected and that that "must have supplied enough reserves" to the banking system on Monday, enabling the Fed to refrain from open market operations then.
But Thrapp also said float, typically higher two days after a holiday, might add enough reserves to the banking system to let the Fed take no action.
Analysts had expected the Fed to add reserves to the banking system on Monday but the Fed stayed out of the market.
"We see a very small add need of $1.5 billion to $2.0 billion a day," said Thrapp. "So there's potential for a small RP today, maybe a small two-day (system repurchase operation)."
Analysts at Standard & Poor's MMS said Treasury deposits at the Fed "were a lot weaker than we expected."
Standard & Poor's MMS analysts said they expected the Fed to add temporary reserves to the banking system on Tuesday through two-day system repurchase agreements.

James Glassman, senior economist at Chase Securities, said an overnight or two-day system repurchase operation would not be surprising. Glassman said Treasury balances at the Fed should be "back to normal today," with balances near $5.2 billion instead of the $3.5 billion reported for Thursday before the three-day holiday weekend.
Federal funds were trading at 5-1/2 percent, the Fed's target for the rate, at mid-morning.
(( E. Freilich, North American Treasury Desk 212-859-1679))
